newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SAAB AB H1 PROFIT RISES 23 PCT.
newsitem.headline: SAAB AB H1 PROFIT RISES 23 PCT.

text.p: Swedish investment group Investor AB said on Thursday its wholly-owned subsidiary Saab AB posted a profit after financial items of 242 million crowns in the first half of 1997 against 197 million a year ago.
It said sales for the aerospace and defence technology group rose 19 percent to 5.34 billion crowns.

Saab swung to a six-month operating profit of 27 million crowns from an operating loss of 83 million as extra allocations and write-downs for commercial aircraft weighed on the first half of 1996, Investor said in a statement.

Order bookings surged to 13.05 billion crowns in the first six months of the year from 3.95 billion in the corresponding year-earlier period. At the end of the period the order backlog amounted to 27.93 billion crowns compared with 19.96 billion.
Sales were also stronger with 12 JAS 39 Gripen fighter aircraft sold in the period compared with eight in the corresponding months the year before.
On the commercial aircraft side 16 Saab 340 planes were delivered, down from 17 a year earlier, and eight Saab 2000 planes, unchanged from the first half of 1996.
"Although demand for regional airliners is strong, business terms continue to be severe," Investor said.
"The preference for jet aircraft has increased: 200 of the total 240 new aircraft for 20-59 passengers ordered during the first half of the year were jets."
The business area Combitech's sales rose mainly through higher sales of Saab Ericsson Space and Saab Marine Electronics. Order bookings were also strong.
"In the Combitech Group, Saab Ericsson Space, Saab Marine Electronics and Telelogic have had very good order bookings," Investor said.
The business area Training Systems boosted sales of laser simulators.
